name: aoa-validation-evidence-graph
proof_question: Can an owner-local claim/evidence graph reduce validation critical-path latency without omitting, weakening, misbinding, or falsely reusing any evidence required by the serial full gate?
origin_need: AbyssOS sessions repeatedly pay long serial validation and retry costs. The optimization must preserve the full fail-closed proof boundary while comparing DAG, worker, sharding, routing, and reuse methods rather than selecting one by assumption.
summary: Compare full serial validation with bounded graph scheduling, pytest worker strategies, static shards, shadow change routing, and exact-identity receipt reuse under no-miss, sufficiency, resource, and real-session constraints.
object_under_evaluation: aoa-sdk owner-local validation evidence planner, runner, manifest, receipts, and scheduling candidates
expected_use_when: Selecting a validation scheduler for aoa-sdk without weakening Repo Validation
Testing the reusable owner-local claim/evidence ABI before any AbyssOS-wide rollout
Evaluating whether partial change routing or receipt reuse is safe enough to leave shadow mode
blind_spot_notes: A local timing win does not prove hosted CI, landing, or end-to-end session benefit.
A green selected subgraph does not prove no-miss routing until seeded positive and negative changes agree with the full serial oracle.
A matching commit alone is insufficient for receipt reuse; manifest, command, inputs, environment, and evidence identity must also match.
The local suite does not grant verdict, scoring, regression, proof doctrine, central adoption, sibling rollout, or publication authority.
Warm caches, host contention, startup variance, and nested pytest processes can invert scheduler rankings and require interleaved repeated trials.

comparison_surface.oracle: the unchanged serial scripts/release_check.py command battery plus its explicit workflow prerequisites
candidates: pytest-xdist loadfile with two and four workers
